triples.evidence: X3D 4.0 export writes creaseAngle from the sharp edges of a smooth-shaded mesh (just under the smallest dihedral angle among them) instead of always pi
Importing an X3D 4.0 scene and exporting it again as X3D 4.0 keeps what used to be lost: light intensity above 1
In Blender 5.x an indexed read of a corner attribute (layer.uv[i].vector, corner_normals[i].vector, color_attributes.active_color.data[i].color) costs time proportional to the size of the collection
New test tests/test_extract_bulk_reads_bpy.py fails on the old code.
X3D 4.0 export with Export animation writes an animated shape key as a CoordinateInterpolator routed into the mesh's Coordinate (set_point), so a morph survives X3D to Blender to X3D.
Before, such a mesh was written as the pose at the current frame and the motion was lost: the Shroud 1532 fold went from 1.5 MB to 0.16 MB. Now it round-trips at 1.56 MB, valid X3D 4.0
A CoordinateInterpolator routed into a Coordinate's set_point imports as shape keys with keyframed values, so a deforming IndexedFaceSet moves in Blender and leaves as glTF morph targets.

An ElevationGrid whose xDimension differs from its zDimension imports as the grid it is: the vertices were numbered x-outer, z-inner while the faces, the per-vertex colours and a default texture mapping all indexed them
Before, a 151 x 121 terrain (the Giza Sphinx-site ground) came in as long vertical fins; square grids were never affected.
Lines survive the X3D 4.0 export: a curve or a mesh that has edges and no faces (what an imported IndexedLineSet becomes in Blender) is written as an IndexedLineSet of polylines.
Before, it produced no geometry, so line-based content (the twelve evidence-graded travel legs of the Shroud journey scene) vanished from the export.
An UnlitMaterial with an emissiveTexture imports as the texture times its emissiveColor (a Mix node set to Multiply), as X_ITE draws it.
A texture's alpha makes the imported surface transparent, as X_ITE draws it: the colour texture's alpha (an UnlitMaterial's emissiveTexture, else the baseTexture) times 1 - transparency
An X3D Switch imports every child, as before, but shows only the one its whichChoice names, as an X3D browser does
Importer reads the Geometry2D nodes Rectangle2D (a quad) and Disk2D (a disc, an annulus or, with equal radii, a circle) in the local XY plane, with texture coordinates; both were skipped before.
